structured_output.content:
Fixed the regression in sqlparse/filters/others.py's StripTrailingSemicolonFilter.process method. The bug was an off-by-one index error: the loop checked `stmt.tokens[-2].value == ';'` instead of `stmt.tokens[-1].value == ';'`, so the trailing semicolon token itself was never detected and stripped (it would only strip whitespace tokens after it, never the semicolon). Changed `stmt.tokens[-2]` to `stmt.tokens[-1]`.

Verified the fix manually: `sqlparse.split('select * from foo;', strip_semicolon=True)` now returns `['select * from foo']` (semicolon stripped) instead of `['select * from foo;']`. This matches the expected behavior described in the bug report (affecting 'split strip semicolon' and 'split strip semicolon procedure' test cases).

No test files were found in the workspace to run directly (no `tests/` directory present), but the fix was confirmed via direct invocation of the affected public API.

Changed `stmt.tokens[-2]` to `stmt.tokens[-1]`.

Verified the fix manually: `sqlparse.split('select * from foo;', strip_semicolon=True)` now returns `['select * from foo']` (semicolon stripped) instead of `['select * from foo;']`. This matches the expected behavior described in the bug report (affecting 'split strip semicolon' and 'split strip semicolon procedure' test cases).

No test files were found in the workspace to run directly (no `tests/` directory present), but the fix was confirmed via direct invocation of the affected public API.
